notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 32% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 11th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 9 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 69% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 54:40 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 4 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 51% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 46:36 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Ilya Solovyov was added to the roster on Oct 20 and has played beside Kris Letang.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

PIT.head: The Penguins have a slight edge
PIT.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Pittsburgh has home-ice advantage and gets Solovyov back. The Bruins can still swing it if they get good looks.

BOS.head: A slightly uphill night for the Bruins
BOS.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Pittsburgh has home-ice advantage and gets Solovyov back. The Bruins’ best way to tip it is getting good looks.

story.head: Clifton returns to Pittsburgh
paras: The Bruins (10-4-1) beat Chicago 5-4 in overtime on Saturday, while the Penguins (5-7-2) lost 5-4 to Montréal the same night. Going in, the Bruins are first in the Atlantic (fourth in the NHL) and the Pens sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 24th).

The Bruins’ record (.700) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.552), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Penguins have played better than their record (.429) says: their chances are worth about .558, and losses in one-goal games have held them back. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Penguins (lowest) and the Bruins (2nd lowest) both sit back rather than chase on the forecheck. The Bruins have had the league’s best goaltending (1st). They also leave the shooting to their forwards (2nd lowest), so the Penguins have the edge over them on shots from defensemen. Boston has allowed 2.40 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. As for the Penguins, they get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). The Bruins could find some good looks against the Penguins, who give up plenty of them.

David Pastrňák (8 G / 11 A / 19 P in 15 GP) leads the Bruins in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. For the Penguins, Erik Karlsson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Evgeni Malkin (6 G / 5 A / 11 P in 13 GP) has a team-high six goals.
Jeremy Swayman (7-3-1 / .912 SV% in 11 GS) has been outstanding for Boston and will likely start. Artūrs Šilovs (5-3-1 / .889 SV% in 9 GS) is in line to start for Pittsburgh.

items.text: Connor Clifton faces Pittsburgh for the first time since leaving.
The Penguins are newly without Elmer Söderblom, and have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk and Bryan Rust for several games.
Pavel Zacha has six goals in nine games against Pittsburgh since 2023-24.
Morgan Geekie has two goals on chances worth about 3.9 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
